'''Mara Jade: Flesh and Blood''' is a six-page feature by Scott Chernoff in ''Star Wars Insider'' 47 (January 2000, pages 52–57). It is the magazine's behind-the-scenes story of Decipher's photographic [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]] for [[Enhanced Jabba's Palace]] — the first flesh-and-blood image of the character. Model [[Shannon Baksa]] (later Shannon McRandle) is on the cover and throughout the shoot.<ref name="wook-47">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_Insider_47 Star Wars Insider 47], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170620212824/http://starwars.wikia.com/wiki/Star_Wars_Insider_47 Wayback, 20 June 2017].</ref><ref name="wook-fab">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mara_Jade:_Flesh_and_Blood Mara Jade: Flesh and Blood], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250418063630/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mara_Jade:_Flesh_and_Blood Wayback, 18 April 2025].</ref>

The feature is part of Decipher's promotion of Enhanced Jabba's Palace, of which Mara Jade was the heavily marketed premium. Decipher's own publisher summary opened "Can you say Mara Jade?" The magazine put a Decipher CCG photoshoot on the cover of Lucasfilm's official fan magazine. That is a substantial promotional effort, even if Mara's later table presence did not match that billing.<ref name="wook-ejp">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Enhanced_Jabba%27s_Palace Enhanced Jabba's Palace], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010202165200/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/spotlight/enhancedjabbaspalace/index.html Decipher Product Spotlight (Wayback, 2 February 2001)].</ref>

[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 Mara Jade cover.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Shannon McRandle as Mara Jade on the cover of ''Star Wars Insider'' 47 (January 2000). Photograph: Mark Atkinson, Otto Studios.<ref name="wook-47" />]]

== Two-page spread ==

Wookieepedia's interior still of the feature is the magazine's opening spread (pages 52–53): Chernoff's article body on the left, Baksa in the black Emperor's Hand costume on the right. The on-image text is the published article, not a caption added later.<ref name="wook-fab" />

[[File:Mara Jade Flesh and Blood.jpg|800px]]

== Star Wars Insider 47 ==

''Star Wars Insider'' 47 is the forty-seventh issue of the official Lucasfilm fan magazine. Published January 2000 (StarWars.com dated the street date 3 January 2000). Editor Jon Bradley Snyder. Publisher The Fan Club, Inc. / Fantastic Media. 82 pages. ISSN 1041-5122.<ref name="wook-47" /><ref name="ia-47">[https://archive.org/details/starwarsinsider_1_to_153_plus_specials Star Wars Insider 1 to 153 plus specials], Internet Archive (issue 047 scan).</ref><ref name="sw-streets">[https://www.starwars.com/community/fanclub/mag/news20000103.html New Star Wars Insider #47 Hits the Streets], StarWars.com (3 January 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20051205134152/https://www.starwars.com/community/fanclub/mag/news20000103.html Wayback, 5 December 2005].</ref>

On 27 October 1999 StarWars.com previewed the upcoming cover as the first official flesh-and-blood image of Mara Jade. Mara would appear on her own Decipher CCG card, but ''Insider'' would print those images first, with an interview about her rise to popularity by creator Timothy Zahn. The issue was scheduled for late December.<ref name="sw-preview">[https://www.starwars.com/community/fanclub/mag/news19991027c/index.html Mara Jade: Flesh and Blood], StarWars.com (27 October 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20110703035710/https://www.starwars.com/community/fanclub/mag/news19991027c/index.html Wayback, 3 July 2011].</ref>

The 3 January 2000 street notice: Chewbacca and Mara Jade (the new Mrs. Luke Skywalker) share the spotlight, and Mara "graces the cover of Insider #47." The cover story has exclusive interviews with Zahn and "the woman tapped to become the first 'flesh and blood' version of Mara, Shannon Baksa."<ref name="sw-streets" />

Wookieepedia's issue contents quote the published blurb:<ref name="wook-47" />

:Finally, an all-out look at the most popular character in the ''Star Wars'' Expanded Universe! Scott Chernoff goes behind the scenes at the photo shoot for Mara Jade's new Decipher card—the first "life-action" rendering of the new Mrs. Skywalker—and talks to character creator Timothy Zahn about the evolution and future of the former Emperor's Hand. It's a Mara Jade blow-out!

== The article ==

Chernoff's byline on page 52. Subhead: "The most popular character in the Expanded Star Wars Universe leaps from the page as Decipher releases the first-ever real-life version of the Emperor's Hand."

=== Pages 52–53 ===

[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 page 52.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Page 52, the article opener.]]
[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 page 53.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Page 53, full-page pose used on [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]].]]

Opener:

:"SHE IS AN ENIGMA. DARK AND LIGHT. ASSASSIN AND ABANDONED. Reserved but powerful. Graceful as a cat, yet tough as nails. A journey from the Emperor's hand to taking the hand of Luke Skywalker as a wife and Jedi Knight. Nobody ever said being Mara Jade was easy."<ref name="ia-47" />

Chernoff dates Mara's first appearance to Timothy Zahn's 1991 novel ''Heir to the Empire''. When ''Insider'' ran a favorite-character poll in 1998 (issue 38), Mara was the only non-movie character to make the list, placing #20, "with one fan boldly writing that Mara is 'by far one of the coolest characters ever to be associated with Star Wars.'"<ref name="ia-47" />

:"Until now. For the first time, Jade fans who have spent the last eight years assimilating various drawings from books and comics with action figures and video game renderings finally have a human face to put to the mysterious character. The face is that of Shannon Baksa, a 30-year-old model from Virginia, and the unlikely occasion is the release of Decipher's newest expansion pack for its Star Wars Customizable Card Game, the Enhanced Jabba's Palace pack, which was scheduled for release in November, 1999."<ref name="ia-47" />

(Decipher's street date for Enhanced Jabba's Palace was 12 January 2000. Chernoff's November 1999 figure is the magazine's contemporary schedule, written before that street date.)<ref name="ejp-011000">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010205143400/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/spotlight/enhancedjabbaspalace/articles/011000.html "Take me to Enhanced Jabba's Palace now!"], Justin Pakes, Decipher Product Spotlight (10 January 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010205143400/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/spotlight/enhancedjabbaspalace/articles/011000.html Wayback, 5 February 2001].</ref>

Decipher creative director Dan Burns, to Chernoff:

:"We were working on the Enhanced Jabba's Palace, and Mara was one of the characters in it, a Power Card, so I thought, 'What about the possibility of fleshing her out?' She's been depicted so many different times in so many different ways, but she's never been filmed."<ref name="ia-47" />

Burns and the creative team used comics, book covers, and action figures, then searched for someone athletic and agile, with "a kind of inner vulnerability that's briefly glimpsed, and a strength, too." With project photographer Mark Atkinson of Otto Studios they found Baksa. Burns: "She seemed to have the agile, catlike quality that Mara Jade has."<ref name="ia-47" />

=== Page 54: the shoot and the printed card ===

[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 page 54.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Page 54. Makeup and costume stills, the printed Enhanced Jabba's Palace card, and Chernoff's Timothy Zahn sidebar.]]

Baksa told Chernoff she had not known the character until she heard Decipher was looking for someone, then "went out and grabbed the comic book and the first three books." She read one and "got hooked," bought green contacts (her eyes are gray), and learned to use them before the interview. "And from the little bit I was able to read before the interview, I could learn to carry myself like her."<ref name="ia-47" />

:"What I got out of what I read was that she was kind of quiet and more observant rather than jumping into the middle of everything, and that she was a very strong woman, physically as well as mentally. I tried to carry myself as if I was very certain of myself, and be quiet and listen to everything they had to say, and then make my remarks about it."<ref name="ia-47" />

Chernoff writes that she then slipped into Mara Jade's black leather catsuit "as well as a different green outfit meant to depict Mara's light side (which will be issued later as another Power Card in the game)." Baksa: "They had it made to fit me exactly, so when I put it on it was easy to become the character. I could completely see Mara Jade walking around in this, so I immediately felt like her."<ref name="ia-47" />

That parenthetical is a contemporary January 2000 source that Decipher intended a Light Side Mara Jade Power Card from the same shoot. Decipher never printed that card. The Players Committee later used the green-costume photograph for Virtual Set 17 [[Mara Jade]]. See [[Unreleased cards]].<ref name="set17">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/light-side-mara-jade-virtual-set-17-spoiler/ Light Side Mara Jade, Virtual Set 17 spoiler], Players Committee (4 December 2021). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230303022134/https://www.starwarsccg.org/light-side-mara-jade-virtual-set-17-spoiler/ Wayback, 3 March 2023].</ref>

Burns collaborated with costume designers from the Virginia Stage Company, "which happens to be across the street from Decipher's Norfolk headquarters," to match what fans had seen in various depictions of Mara. The magazine prints the finished [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]] card on this page.<ref name="ia-47" />

The yellow lower half is Chernoff's interview with Zahn ("When Tim Zahn Met Mara Jade"). Zahn calls a hired actor for a character he created unique in his experience: "cover art turns them into pictures, but not into a real live person." He would look for green eyes, red hair, and a dancer's figure, "and that's about as far as I've ever really visualized."<ref name="ia-47" />

=== Page 55: Who is Mara Jade? ===

[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 page 55.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Page 55. Baksa in the green Light Side costume, captioned "LIGHT SIDE: Mara Jade, Jedi Knight."]]

Burns had a lightsaber made "based on some sketches used in the Dark Horse comics, so we could get it as close to accurate as possible. (The lit part of the lightsaber in the pictures comes from a film still of Luke Skywalker.)"<ref name="ia-47" />

:"It was a really big production for just a little card, but I felt it was very important to get this one right."<ref name="ia-47" />

Baksa said she saw the original ''Star Wars'' 15 times as a kid and had a huge crush on Han ("sorry, Luke"). She was thrilled with her weapon: "Oh, please—they had a lightsaber made for me!" "That was the coolest thing. I felt like a little kid when they handed me that. I had to practice for a few minutes—that thing was heavy. We played with it all day. I had fun knocking over the lights."<ref name="ia-47" />

A model since age 12, she said the project meant more than most of her previous jobs. "When they told me my picture had to pass through Lucasfilm, that kind of told me, OK this is big."<ref name="ia-47" />

The right-hand portrait is the green military jumpsuit with a blue blade. Caption: "LIGHT SIDE: Mara Jade, Jedi Knight." A "Who is Mara Jade?" fact box lists name Mara Jade Skywalker, affiliation Empire then New Republic, rank Jedi Knight, weapon "magenta lightsaber; Luke's blue lightsaber from ''The Empire Strikes Back''," vehicles Jade's Fire and Hunter's Luck, quote "Ask me if I care" (''Heir to the Empire'').<ref name="ia-47" />

=== Page 56: Saber Rattler ===

[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 page 56.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Page 56. Chernoff's closer, plus the rest of the Zahn interview.]]

The green-costume quote continues onto this page: "It's just so cool with how much ''Star Wars'' meant to me when I was young. I collected those cards for years—and I can't believe I ever let them go. I had every single one!"<ref name="ia-47" />

Now that she ''is'' a card, Baksa said she is glad she was introduced to the Emperor's Hand:

:"I like that she's a no nonsense character—she's taking care of business. I like the fact that she's a bad guy but not really. I think she has a really good heart, she's just been taught poorly. She's beautiful, she's strong, she's a character that has a long way to go. She started out being one thing and you're going through this big life change with her. Even though she starts as a bad guy, she's really likable—I liked her right away."<ref name="ia-47" />

Burns:

:"In the first three films, there are so few women except for Leia, so I think that's the appeal to her—plus the fact that she is struggling with her own duality of nature, such as Luke has."<ref name="ia-47" />

:"It was exciting, because everything else has been an illustrated or figure depiction of her, so to have a photographic depiction of her is the top of the canon. You never know—she might be appearing at a Con near you."<ref name="ia-47" />

Baksa: "I would love to do that. It sounds like the greatest fun—to become Mara Jade for a day." Chernoff's closer: "Hey, nobody said being Mara Jade was easy, but we didn't say it couldn't be fun."<ref name="ia-47" />

She did appear at conventions as Mara Jade, including [[DecipherCon 1999]] and [[DecipherCon 2000]].

=== Page 57: Superstar bibliography ===

[[File:Star Wars Insider 47 page 57.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Page 57. "Mara Jade: Superstar!" bibliography.]]

The last page is a Mara Jade bibliography (novels, comics, short stories, games, action figures). Under '''GAMES''' the magazine lists:

:STAR WARS CUSTOMIZABLE CARD GAME: JABBA'S PALACE ENHANCED (1999, Decipher)<ref name="ia-47" />

That is the magazine treating Enhanced Jabba's Palace as Mara's game appearance, dated 1999 in the bibliography (the product streeted 12 January 2000).

== Enhanced Jabba's Palace promotion ==

Decipher marketed the set around Mara. Wookieepedia quotes the publisher's summary:<ref name="wook-ejp" />

:Can you say Mara Jade? Finally, the fabled character (from the Timothy Zahn novels and 'Tales From Jabba's Palace') comes alive as one of the 12 new Premium cards for this enhanced set.

:Each of the four Enhanced tuck boxes contains 4 booster packs from the original Jabba's Palace expansion set plus 3 new Premium cards. You'll know exactly which 3 Premium cards you're getting in each EJP tuck box because the die-cut front will reveal the face card (one of the four different face cards).

On 17 December 1999 Justin Pakes's Decipher Product Spotlight "Are You Ready To Return To The Palace?" opened the card-by-card preview with Mara:<ref name="ejp-121799">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010205144100/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/spotlight/enhancedjabbaspalace/articles/121799.html Are You Ready To Return To The Palace?], Justin Pakes, Decipher Product Spotlight (17 December 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010205144100/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/spotlight/enhancedjabbaspalace/articles/121799.html Wayback, 5 February 2001].</ref>

:"Where else could you start your examination of EJP but with the renowned Mara? Our first meeting with this lethal lady is after her training with The Emperor, and on assignment to track down and dispatch Luke Skywalker. She infiltrates Jabba's Palace and awaits her prey..."

Pakes called her "nothing less than a Dark Side main character" on statistics alone (ability 5, power 6 with Emperor, forfeit 7, deploy 5), then walked duel text, spy/Undercover, and the first Dark Side dual Alien/Imperial persona so she would not suspend Scum And Villainy. The same article spoiled [[Mara Jade's Lightsaber]]. Attendees at [[DecipherCon 1999]] had already seen some EJP cards in the Art Gallery.<ref name="ejp-121799" />

On 10 January 2000, two days before the 12 January street date, Pakes listed all twelve premiums. [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]] is the visible facing card of her die-cut pack, with [[You Can Either Profit By This... / Or Be Destroyed]] and [[Bossk With Mortar Gun]].<ref name="ejp-011000" />

== Oversized convention cards ==

Decipher later printed two 5×7 convention premiums that use Baksa's likeness. They are show premiums, not playable deck cards in the usual sense. Collectors could spend $20 at the Decipher convention store. See [[Oversized cards]].<ref name="bgg-42">[https://boardgamegeek.com/filepage/33565/star-wars-ccg-complete-card-list-42 Star Wars CCG Complete Card List 4.2], Whaleyland, BoardGameGeek (22 August 2012). The 4.2 checklist lists both oversized Mara titles as "Spend $20 or more at Decipher Store at conventions."</ref>

[[File:Oversized Mara Jade The Emperor's Hand.jpg|thumb|left|280px|5×7 oversized [[Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand]], signed "Shannon Baksa as Mara Jade / San Diego." Photograph of a copy offered by CategoryOne Games.<ref name="c1g-mara">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-misc_sw_items/mara_jade_oversized_signed_by_shannon_baksa_in_san_diego/97531 Mara Jade [Oversized] signed by Shannon Baksa in San Diego], CategoryOne Games. Preserved copy: [http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=11259 Premium Oversize Card, Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand], Star Wars Collectors Archive (Duncan Jenkins, 5×7, year 2000).</ref>]]
[[File:Oversized Mara Jade The Emperor's Hand scale.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The 5×7 held next to the regular-size Enhanced Jabba's Palace original.<ref name="ccg-collector">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=frvqLMqMc14 Guide - SW:CCG Collection - Oversized/Undersized Cards], The CCG Collector (29 November 2015). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-frvqLMqMc14 Internet Archive].</ref>]]

The Dark Side oversized is a 5×7 of the Enhanced Jabba's Palace card (copyright 2000). Star Wars Collectors Archive item 11259 (photo Duncan Jenkins) catalogs it as CCG Show Premium, 5×7, licensee Decipher, year 2000.<ref name="swca-11259">[http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=11259 Premium Oversize Card, Mara Jade, The Emperor's Hand], Star Wars Collectors Archive. Description and photo: Duncan Jenkins.</ref>

[[File:Oversized Mara Jade Corran Horn Talon Karrde.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Unsigned 5×7 ''•Mara Jade & •Corran Horn & •Talon Karrde''. Lore is printed; the game-text box is blank for autographs.<ref name="c1g-group">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-misc_sw_items/mara_jade__corran_horn__talon_karde_oversized/48055 Mara Jade & Corran Horn & Talon Karde [Oversized]], CategoryOne Games.</ref>]]

The Light Side group oversized (copyright 2001) is unique among the 5×7s: it has no normal-sized counterpart. Baksa is Mara; Michael A. Stackpole portrayed Corran Horn and Timothy Zahn portrayed Talon Karrde on the [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] cards, and the three were shot together at that session for a possible later card.<ref name="tfn-rfd">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Yaruas_RFD_Report_622628_72011.asp Yarua's RFD Report (6.22–6.28)], TheForce.net (23 June 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20150215035122/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/yaruas_rfd_report_622628_72011.asp Wayback, 15 February 2015].</ref>

Radio Free Decipher (22 June 2001), as reported by Yarua on TheForce.net the next day: Decipher would be at Origins, San Diego, GenCon, Wizard World, and DragonCon with Baksa, Stackpole, and Zahn among the guests, and would make available a special oversized card for those autographs:<ref name="tfn-rfd" />

:Corran Horn & Mara Jade & Talon Karrde Destiny: 3 / Power: 8 Ability: 5 Deploy: 8 Forfeit: 9 / Pilots & Warriors / No Game Text (you'll need room for autographs!)

The printed card matches those stats. Title line: •Mara Jade & •Corran Horn & •Talon Karrde. Lore: "Each driven by a dubious past, these scoundrels now plan for the greater good of the New Republic. Found in the strangest places." Power 8, Ability 5, Force-Sensitive. Deploy 8, Forfeit 9. Pilot and Warrior icons. The game-text box is blank. The back has the Rebel Alliance symbol with decipher.com and starwars.com.<ref name="c1g-group" /><ref name="nkg-group">[https://www.nobleknight.com/P/2148343730/Oversized-Promo---Mara-Jade-and-Corran-Horn-and-Talon-Karrde Oversized Promo - Mara Jade & Corran Horn & Talon Karrde], Noble Knight Games (5×7×.1").</ref>

[[File:Oversized Mara Jade Corran Horn Talon Karrde signed.jpg|thumb|left|260px|The same 5×7 signed by Timothy Zahn (8/31/01), Shannon Baksa as Mara Jade, and Michael A. Stackpole — the use Decipher described on Radio Free Decipher. Photograph: Noble Knight Games.<ref name="nkg-group" />]]
[[File:Oversized Mara Jade Corran Horn Talon Karrde back.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Back of the group oversized: Rebel Alliance symbol, decipher.com, starwars.com.<ref name="nkg-group" />]]

Star Wars Collectors Archive item 11260 catalogs the group card as CCG Show Premium, 5×7, 2001.<ref name="swca-11260">[http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=11260 Premium Oversize Card, Mara Jade, Corran Horn & Talon Karrde], Star Wars Collectors Archive.</ref>
